title: Interleaved cold-cache stress scratchpad
content:
Goal: explore worst-case P99 behavior when a small fraction of requests repeatedly hit cold KV-cache items interleaved with hot cached requests. Trying to reproduce a multi-tenant tail event we saw in staging (2025-01-22) where 3% of requests triggered cold-decoding and p99 spiked ~4x for ~30s.

Quick background/context:
- Hypothesis: interleaved arrivals that bounce between hot and cold state cause the runtime to thrash between fast path and slow decode/IO, invalidating batching/coalescing heuristics and stalling other inflight tokens.
- Environment: single-node dedicated test cluster (4x A10X equivalent GPUs), baseline runtime v0.83.1 with new KV-cache eviction code disabled (control vs experiment later).

Experiment design:
- Two synthetic arrival classes: HOT (80% of qps) and COLD (20% of qps). HOT queries are short prefix continuations that hit primed KV; COLD queries are first-time prefixes pointing to large segment requiring quantized decode + disk spill.
- Interleaving patterns tested:
  * uniform-mix: Poisson arrivals with p=0.2 COLD per request (baseline).
  * clustered-cold: bursts of 40-80 COLD requests every 20s, otherwise HOT.
  * alternating-steady: strict alternating HOT/COLD at 50%/50% but reduced QPS so system not saturated (control for deterministic interference).
- QPS swept: 100, 300, 700, 1200 (node capacity ~1400). Each run 3m steady-state after 30s ramp, collect per-request latencies and kernel traces.
- Metrics recorded: p50/p90/p95/p99, tail-by-arrival-type, KV cache hit-rate, batch sizes, GPU occupancy, queue lengths, stall durations (time waiting on disk or decode), and end-to-end token latency breakdowns.

Commands / workload generator snippets (local harness):
- python simtrade.py --pattern clustered-cold --qps 700 --ratio 0.2 --duration 210 
- workload generator tags requests with header X-TEST-CASE: interleaved-coldcache-elodie

Results (notes from runs):
1) uniform-mix @700 QPS (control): p50 12ms, p95 28ms, p99 120ms. KV-hit-rate ~84%. Observed occasional 600-900ms cold spikes (~0.6% of requests) correlated to disk reads for quantized shards. Batch sizes consistent (avg token batch 14).
2) clustered-cold @700 QPS: p50 14ms, p95 35ms, p99 520ms. KV-hit-rate avg 78% but dips to 55% during cold bursts. GPU occupancy dropped by ~12% for 2-6s after each burst. Notably, many HOT requests adjacent to bursts show increased latency (p99 for HOT subset rose from 75ms to 420ms).
3) alternating-steady @300 QPS (50/50 synthetic): p50 18ms, p95 46ms, p99 150ms. Even though below saturation, alternation caused batch formation to break: many batches had mixed token types forcing decoding path fallback and increasing per-token overhead.
4) high-load clustered-cold @1200 QPS: system experienced congestion cascades. p99 > 2s, visible queue buildup; several kernels queued waiting on decode I/O. Significant fairness inversion where tenants with mostly HOT traffic were impacted more than expected.

Trace observations and root-cause signals:
- KV-cache eviction + rehydration path adds synchronous decode+disk latency that blocks worker threads used by fast path when scheduling not isolated.
- Batching heuristic is greedy: it tries to accumulate tokens up to target but does not separate requests by expected compute class; mixed batches cause worst-case slowdowns.
- Small micro-locks around cache-layer stats become hot under bursts, adding 1-2ms per request but magnified across thousands of requests during a burst.

Quick mitigation ideas to try (next runs):
- Smart partitioned batches: separate batch queues by "hotness" tag computed at admission time (fast path vs rehydrate path).
- Limit max concurrent rehydrate jobs per-GPU and throttle them via a separate worker pool so they don't steal CPU/GPU slots from HOT path.
- Prefetch heuristic: if a request is likely cold (by prefix signature), prefetch asynchronously (background) before the main request arrives — test with 50ms lead window.
- Backpressure shaping: detect clustered cold bursts, temporarily widen batching timeout for HOT lane to absorb jitter instead of immediate fallback to slow path.
- Reduce lock contention: move per-thread counters or use sharded counters for per-bucket stats.

Planned experiment matrix (next steps):
- Run with partitioned batch queues enabled (branch: batch-split-hot-cold) vs control. Measure same QPS points, same patterns.
- Run with rehydrate-thread-limiter=2 (config) to observe HOT tail improvement.
- A/B run enabling asynchronous prefetch (best-effort) for lookahead prefixes.

Data excerpt (raw sample from clustered-cold @700 QPS run, 2025-02-12 14:22 UTC):
- Total requests: 126,412 over 3m
- Observed cold rehydrates: 24,301 (19.2%)
- p99 overall: 520ms
- p99 HOT-only: 420ms
- p99 COLD-only: 1.1s
- Avg batch size before burst: 15 tokens; during burst: 6 tokens

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the rehydrate code doing a sync GPU memcpy that blocks the fast path, or is it a CPU-side decode causing scheduling pressure? Need microkernel traces.
- Why does lock contention spike exactly at burst boundaries? Correlation with per-shard stats update frequency, likely code-path updating global LRU.
- Can we patch admission controller to tag potential cold requests cheaply without expensive signature ops? Maybe using a tiny bloom filter of known-hot prefixes.

Short-term recommendations for staging to reduce customer impact:
- Turn on conservative limit for concurrent rehydrate jobs (per-node) so we don't see full occupation swings.
- Temporarily increase batching timeout for HOT lane by +8ms during suspected bursts.
- Add telemetry to explicitly tag cold-rehydrate events and emit a sampled trace to correlate with p99 spikes.

Notes to self (experiment hygiene):
- Label runs with header X-TEST-CASE and upload traces to GH-portal benchmark artifact group 347.
- Save raw kernel traces to s3://redwood-ci/bench/traces/elodie/ (include run metadata json).
- Reproduce on 2-node dedicated cluster to check multi-node mitigation effects.

TL;DR: interleaved cold requests — especially clustered bursts — amplify p99 by introducing decoding/disk work that steals execution from hot fast-path due to batching and scheduling coupling. Partitioned batching + bounded rehydrate workers look promising.

TODOs:
- [ ] Run partitioned-batching vs control across QPS sweep (assigned Mina).
- [ ] Add per-request "likely-cold" prefetch experiment (assigned Ravi).
- [ ] Capture full microkernel traces for next clustered run (assigned Elodie).

Random scratch ideas:
- Consider a micro-admission gate that probabilistically samples requests into a prefetch queue (cheap hash test) to warm likely-cold items.
- Explore moving bulky decode off-GPU to a node-local pre-warm pool so GPUs remain dedicated to fast token generation.

End of scratchpad.
